elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: The Company may assign this Agreement without HDI's consent to an affiliate

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets
elements.evidence: or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Company

elements.element: Consent not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: and may not assign this Agreement to a competitor of the Company

elements.element: No Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: HDI shall have no right to terminate this Agreement upon a change of control of the Company.

elements.element: Mutual right to assign to successors
elements.evidence: HDI may not assign this Agreement without the prior written consent of the Company (no unilateral successor right for Vendor)
No notice mechanic appears in the inserted text.

elements.element: Consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld

reasons: All six atomic preferred elements are expressly satisfied by the single inserted sentence-set: Customer affiliate assignment, Customer M&A/asset-sale successor assignment, Vendor consent requirement, reasonableness standard, absolute competitor bar, and no Vendor termination right on Customer change of control.
The locked target level (preferred) is complete, so the fallback's mutual successor-assignment-with-notice construct is irrelevant and correctly absent (no impermissible mixing of levels).
Minimal: the original 10.3 is untouched and the fix is a concise insertion addressing the absent consent standard; no whole-clause rewrite, no new exceptions, no boilerplate.
Intent preserved: the binding-on-successors sentence remains effective, all defined terms (HDI, Company) are the document's own aliases, and no dangling mechanic or contradiction is introduced.
